title: Counting and grouping with Dictionary
summary: Tally things in one pass, find the first unique item, and group anagrams by a shared key.

steps.title: The counting pattern
body: Counting how often each thing appears is one of the most useful patterns in programming. A `Dictionary<TKey, int>` maps each item to its count:
`GetValueOrDefault` returns 0 for a key not yet seen, so the first sighting stores 1. One pass, `O(n)`.
Watch the dictionary grow as the trace counts the letters of `banana`.

steps.prompt: Which word is most common? What does this print?
code: foreach (var w in "to be or not to be to".Split(' '))
steps.explain: `to` appears three times; the distinct words are `to`, `be`, `or`, `not`.

steps.prompt: `counts` has no entry for `"zebra"`. What does `counts["zebra"]++` do?
steps.explain: `++` has to **read** the value first, and reading a missing key with the indexer throws. That is why the pattern uses `GetValueOrDefault`. Writing with the indexer (`counts[k] = 1`) never throws.

steps.title: Grouping by a key
body: To group items, map a **shared key** to a list. Anagrams (`"listen"`, `"silent"`) contain the same letters, so sorting their letters gives the same key: `"eilnst"`.
`TryGetValue` does the lookup once and hands back the list, so you can add to it directly.

steps.prompt: Group people's names by their first letter.
steps.explain: Store the **same** list object you just created, so the `list.Add` below adds to the one in the dictionary.

items: Has this email address signed up already?

steps.title: First unique character
prompt: Write `char FirstUnique(string s)`: the first character that appears **exactly once**, or `'_'` if there is none.
Two passes: count every character, then walk the string again and return the first with a count of 1.
solution: foreach (var c in s) counts[c] = counts.GetValueOrDefault(c) + 1;
foreach (var c in s) if (counts[c] == 1) return c;
template: var dojoBig = new string('a', 300_000) + "z" + new string('b', 300_000);
hints: Second loop over `s` (not over the dictionary): return the first `c` with `counts[c] == 1`.

steps.title: Group anagrams
prompt: - Words with the same letters go in the same group.
- Groups appear in the order their **first** word appears; words inside a group keep their input order.
A `Dictionary<string, List<string>>` adds keys in insertion order when nothing is removed, so `groups.Values` comes out in first-seen order.
template: string DojoShow(List<List<string>> g) => string.Join(" | ", g.Select(x => string.Join(",", x)));
Dojo.Eq("groups the example", "tea,eat,ate | tan,nat | bat", DojoShow(GroupAnagrams(new[] { "tea", "eat", "tan", "ate", "nat", "bat" })));
Dojo.Eq("no words, no groups", "", DojoShow(GroupAnagrams(new string[0])));
Dojo.Eq("different lengths never match", "ab,ba | aab", DojoShow(GroupAnagrams(new[] { "ab", "aab", "ba" })));
hints: The key is the word's letters sorted: `new string(word.OrderBy(c => c).ToArray())`.
Use the `TryGetValue` pattern to fetch or create each group's list, then `return groups.Values.ToList();`.
